evidence.estrutura: Otunbayeva served within Kyrgyzstan's post-Soviet constitutional institutions and led a transitional presidency. She supports functioning national institutions but has no signature federalism doctrine.
evidence.representacao: Her political career includes opposition politics, parliament, a transitional presidency and work connected to democratic transition. This strongly supports representative and plural political institutions.
evidence.poder: Her role in post-authoritarian transition and later civic initiatives supports institutional checks, civilian government and resistance to arbitrary concentration of power.
evidence.imigracao: Her diplomatic and UN work is internationally oriented, but the reviewed sources do not establish a distinctive immigration or assimilation program.
evidence.diplomacia: Foreign-minister, ambassadorial and senior UN roles define her career. This very strongly supports diplomacy, mediation and multilateral cooperation.
evidence.intervencao: Her UN and mediation work favors negotiated and international-institutional responses rather than unilateral military intervention.
evidence.economia: Her political record is broadly reformist and post-Soviet mixed-market rather than socialist state ownership or laissez-faire. Use a moderate market-oriented developmental placement.
evidence.controle: She supports state capacity and reform but not command planning. Use low-to-moderate economic control.
evidence.comercio: Her internationalist and reform-oriented career supports economic openness, though no specific tariff doctrine is established.
evidence.religiao: Her public career is secular, diplomatic and constitutional rather than religiously governed.
evidence.moral: Her civic, educational and international work supports women's participation, pluralism and moderate social liberalism.
evidence.tecnologia: Her public profile emphasizes diplomacy, education and institutions more than technology. Use a moderate pragmatic placement.
